bullets.title: Ryan Holiday
Johns Hopkins, Yale, and NYU are teaming up to tackle a key bottleneck that will arise as psychedelics come to market
bullets.creator: Yeji Jesse Lee
bullets.note:
([@jesse\_yeji](https://twitter.com/jesse_yeji)).**This has been in the works for a while, and I couldn’t be more excited.** Here are a few snippets from the above piece: “As psychedelics treatments move closer to regulatory approval, there’s an issue looming in the industry: the lack of trained professionals who can handle such powerful compounds. … The goal is to have the curriculum certified by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education, which would create a pathway to make the program available to medical schools as an accredited specialty all across the country. … The idea is that the program will be designed in a way so that parts of the curriculum can help train other healthcare professionals—like therapists, nurses, and physician assistants—and even be provided as material in medical schools.”  
  
[The Saisei Foundation](https://saiseifoundation.org/), which I started in 2018, is thrilled to be involved. For the official release from the Yale School of Medicine, please read “[Grant Supports Development of Training for Psychiatrists in Psychedelic Medicine](https://medicine.yale.edu/psychiatry/news-article/grant-supports-development-of-training-for-psychiatrists-in-psychedelic-medicine/).” Special thanks to Carey and Claudia Turnbull for quarterbacking this and to the institutions jointly developing the program: the [Yale University Program for Psychedelic Science](https://medicine.yale.edu/psychiatry/research/programs/clinical_people/psychedelic/), the [Johns Hopkins Center for Psychedelic and Consciousness Research](https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/psychiatry/research/psychedelics-research.html), and the [NYU Langone Health Center for Psychedelic Medicine](https://med.nyu.edu/departments-institutes/psychiatry/research/center-psychedelic-medicine).
